    Portal node

    A Portal owns a global route. It has no Enter port and is checked before outputs on the active UI node. In 0.4.0 it is also the destination resolved by a Send Signal node.

    Portal Condition

    Setting Description
    Type Signal or Toggle
    Signal Address Database or Custom when Type is Signal
    Database Signal Signal catalog Category / Key
    Custom Signal Case-sensitive graph-local string
    Toggle Address Toggle catalog Category / Key
    Toggle Value On or Off
    History Push, Replace, or Back
    Output Required route to exactly one UI or Action chain

    For Send Signal routing, Address Type and value must match exactly. Database Default / Home does not match Custom Home even though their visible names are similar.

    Push stores the previous screen when the route reaches a UI. Replace changes UI without modifying history. Back runs connected Actions and then requests history navigation instead of entering the connected UI.

    Portal conditions must be unique by Type, Address Type, address, and Toggle value. Empty Custom values and invalid Database keys are rejected.

    Caution

    A matching Portal has global priority. Reusing a local Signal address in a Portal can make the active UI's own output appear unresponsive.
